title: Testing the parallel read_csv path: force it, place chunk boundaries, assert it was used
answers: how to test parallel read_csv on a small file
how to put a chunk boundary at a specific byte in a test
test passes but parallel path silently fell back to serial
body:
Tests are in pandas/tests/io/parser/test_parallel_read.py.
- To force the parallel path, monkeypatch `pandas.io.parsers.readers._PARALLEL_READ_MIN_BYTES` to 1 and use `pd.option_context("mode.max_threads", N)` with N>=2. Get the serial expectation with max_threads=1 (or engine="python").
- `_read_forced_parallel` / the TestReadCsvParallel helper now call `pytest.fail` (not skip) when the parallel read returns None. A silent fallback is a test failure.
- `_track_parallel(monkeypatch)` records outcomes: "used", "declined" (fell back to serial) or "raised". Assert `outcomes == ["used"]` so that a parity test cannot pass just by falling back.
- To place a boundary: `_find_data_start_offset(path, 0, 0)`, then `_find_chunk_byte_offsets(path, n_chunks, data_start, n_workers=...)` to get the offset and overwrite bytes there. `_spy_on_chunk_offsets` plus `_assert_chunk_starts_at` confirm where the split happened.
- Mark tests that rely on spies or worker behaviour `@pytest.mark.skipif(WASM, ...)`, because WASM always reads serially.
